highlights.title: Amazon’s new Kindles appear to have a light leak problem
highlights.summary: Some users are reporting that the new Kindles have a light leak issue that is especially apparent when using dark mode. The latest base-model Kindles have a flush bezel that gives them a sleek appearance and looks great… as long as you keep the lights on.
body: Reddit users are reporting shadows and visible LEDs around screen edge of new Kindles.

In some cases, users see shadows around the edges of the screen, or even visible LED strips. The issue appears to affect both the plastic and aluminum models in all colors. Some minor glowing around the edges might be a byproduct of the combination of front lighting and a flush screen. But Reddit users say images shared there show something more dramatic that appears to be a defect.

Good e-Reader says that Amazon is aware of the issue and has confirmed that a manufacturing issue may have led to defects in the current batch of Kindles. However, when contacted by The Verge, the company declined to provide an on-the-record statement.

highlights.title: Antonelli casts further doubt over performance of Mercedes upgrades
highlights.summary: World Championship leader Kimi Antonelli cast further doubt over the performance of Mercedes' recent upgrade package as he explained his car was "very difficult" to drive during Sprint Qualifying in Singapore.
body: After the long-awaited upgrades failed to deliver improved performance when they debuted at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Mercedes decided to compare different specifications of the car in Singapore.

Antonelli is running the latest version, which included an additional front wing that had not been available in Malaysia, while George Russell is running the pre-Malaysia version of the car that he won the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in last month.

The early evidence was concerning for Mercedes as Russell finished second to Max Verstappen in the shortened qualifying session, with Antonelli more than half a second down on his team-mate in seventh.
Asked whether he was surprised by the performance, Antonelli said: "Yes and no, to be fair. Already in FP1 I was struggling.

highlights.title: Trump’s attempt to rename AI is looking awfully artificial
highlights.summary: President Donald Trump has a knack for turning words against his enemies. His first successful presidential run was built on monikers like "Little Marco" and "Crooked Hillary"; he changed "fake news" from a phrase describing scammy media outlets to a derogatory term for the press at large.
body: A ‘super’ new euphemism probably isn’t enough to make Americans forget their concerns about AI.

Changes have been swift. The US Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), already a rebrand of the AI Safety Institute, has been renamed the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI). Justice Department press releases have been modified to include the phrase, trumpeting that a man who flooded streaming platforms with AI-generated songs between 2017 and 2024 committed “Super Intelligence-Assisted Music Streaming Fraud.” On Thursday, Trump declared that “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, ‘Artificial Intelligence,’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!”

highlights.title: High Console Prices Push Playstation and Xbox Sales to New Lows
highlights.summary: As an ongoing component crisis continues to drive up console prices, gaming hardware sales are tanking. According to new U.S. retail data from Circana, Xbox hardware sales were down 33% year-to-date in August compared to this point in 2025.
body: In August, PlayStation unit sales fell 11% year over year, bringing them to the lowest August total since 2013. Xbox sales declined even more aggressively, down 31% for the lowest August since 2020. Nintendo also took a hit, down 15% from August last year. This certainly isn’t the first time we’ve heard that console sales are down. Circana previously reported similarly grim data for July.

All three major console manufacturers have raised hardware prices over the last year and a half. Microsoft’s Xbox Series X and S have had multiple price increases, with the Xbox Series X now going for $799.99, which is $300 more than at launch. The base PS5 went from $499 to $549.99 in August 2025, before getting bumped another $100 in April 2026. The Nintendo Switch 2 received a $50 increase this past September.

highlights.title: Microsoft tries to spark new life into Windows
highlights.summary: When Microsoft released Windows 11 five years ago, it felt like an operating system that was still being renovated, a work in progress. You'd think by now that those renovations would be complete, with Microsoft turning its attention to Windows 12.
body: At a Windows and Surface event this week, Microsoft laid out its plan to bring AI agents to Windows, including hybrid intelligence that lets Windows take advantage of free local models instead of expensive cloud ones. “I think today is the day we’ll start talking and thinking about the frontier ecosystem taking maybe slightly different contours,” said Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.

After trying to sell businesses on a new Copilot last month, Nadella took a similar approach for his vision of agents and hybrid intelligence for Windows. It was so similar that when he mentioned the security, identity, and management aspects of Microsoft’s platform for securing agents, it almost seemed like he was pitching businesses again instead of AI developers, creatives, and just regular Windows users.

After a somewhat dizzying start, Windows chief Pavan Davuluri appeared onstage to try and explain why agents and hybrid intelligence are so important for Windows users. There were demos of GitHub Copilot coding locally without expensive cloud tokens; a long list of models that can now run locally; examples of agents like OpenClaw, Hermes, and Perplexity; and even deeper integration of Copilot in Windows.

highlights.title: Street Fighter Movie Officially Reveals Its Big Animated Twist
highlights.summary: The creators of the new Street Fighter movie have been sitting on a secret: A surprising amount of the film is told through traditional 2D animation, one of the film's many throwbacks to the '90s.
body: For a movie that is steeped in '90s sights and sounds, the use of sequences inspired by Japanese animation to tell parts of Street Fighter's story makes sense. It's a way to avoid being "cheesy" during key emotional moments, according to Street Fighter director and co-writer Kitao Sakurai.

The new Street Fighter movie uses animation almost exclusively during flashbacks. These sequences touch on Ken and Ryu's training under their sensei, Master Gouken (played by Don Lee). Street Fighter actually opens with an animated sequence that recounts the first World Warrior tournament and the history of two great rivalries in Street Fighter lore.
Speaking with Sakurai, I asked why the filmmaker decided to insert 2D animation into the otherwise live-action production.

"When we were writing it, we knew that we needed to understand the sort of emotional backstories of Ken and Ryu and what led them to this place, because that's really the heart of the story," Sakurai explained. "Traditionally, if you're gonna do these flashback sequences, you need to make a choice whether to [either] de-age the actors or to hire child actors, and with the tone that we were going for, none of that felt right."

highlights.title: ‘Mystery Science Theater 3000: The RiffTrax Experiments’: Behind the Scenes of the Satellite of Love
highlights.summary: In a cozy suburb of Minneapolis, a guy in a blue jumpsuit is once again stuck aboard a space station with his robot pals, watching the worst movies ever made. To paraphrase the show’s catchy theme song, if you’re wondering how that works, it’s just a TV show, so you should really just relax. In
body: Joel Hodgson created and starred as that guy forced to screen cheesy flicks; he left mid-run and was replaced by Michael J. Nelson. After the show wrapped, Nelson and fellow “MST3K” writer-stars Kevin Murphy and Bill Corbett took the basic idea and launched their own version, RiffTrax, which started as a website and branched out into live performances and its own FAST channel.
Then, in 2017, Hodgson revived “MST3K” at Netflix and launched a related streaming platform called The Gizmoplex, but the RiffTrax team wasn’t involved.

That all changed this year. In January, Hodgson sold his ownership in the series to Radial Entertainment and once again departed. Radial then recruited the RiffTrax team to return for four new episodes. “Mystery Science Theater 3000: The RiffTrax Experiments” was born.

The transition of “MST3K” to Radial allowed the company to approach the RiffTrax team (who hadn’t been formally involved in any new interations of the show since 1999) about joining forces, which they were eager to do. Fans were in: They raised $2.7 million in a Kickstarter campaign to fund the revival, and “The RiffTrax Experiments” were off and running.

highlights.title: What happens to your pets when you die?
highlights.summary: Without a proper plan – whether in a trust or will – your beloved companion could face an animal shelter or worse. The idea of making a will may be uncomfortable, but routine. Ensuring that your family and estate is taken care of is a kindness.
body: Sometimes, “somebody wants to set up a trust with substantial money in it”, he said. But more typically, the client wants to ensure “the right person” gets the dog or cat – but has no idea how best to do it.
As the person in charge of your pet’s livelihood, you can (and should) try to get something on paper that makes sense.

“Pets rely entirely on human care. Without a plan, they face stress, shelter, surrender or unnecessary euthanasia during an already chaotic time,” said Peter Klein, the founder of the therapy referral website Seek a Psych and a London-based cognitive behavioral therapist in private practice.

According to a report from Best Friends Animal Society, a non-profit advocacy group working to achieve no-kill statuses for shelters around the United States, 12.4% of the 4.74 million cats and dogs that entered the shelter system in 2025 ended up there due to owner illness or death.

highlights.title: The DOJ Is Weighing Perjury Charges Against Cassidy Hutchinson
highlights.summary: The Justice Department is considering a perjury and obstruction-of-justice case against Cassidy Hutchinson, a former White House aide who testified against Donald Trump to the January 6 committee.
body: Federal prosecutors have been weighing a perjury and obstruction-of-justice case against Cassidy Hutchinson, who implicated President Donald Trump in the January 6 Capitol riot in testimony four years ago, according to two sources familiar with the matter.

The efforts mark the Justice Department’s intent to proceed against Hutchinson, a former aide to ex-Trump White House chief of staff Mark Meadows, though prosecutors are not expected to ask a federal grand jury in Washington to return an indictment until at least after the midterm elections, the sources say.

Hutchinson testified as a star witness to the committee that investigated the riot, recounting that Trump encouraged his supporters to march to the Capitol even though he knew many were armed. She sat for several interviews in addition to her public testimony, where she recalled hearing that Trump had lunged at one of his Secret Service agents after being told he could not join his supporters at the Capitol.

highlights.summary: Principal denies bias towards Antonelli over Russell. Verstappen takes pole in sprint qualifying in Singapore. Toto Wolff has condemned accusations of bias in how he has managed his drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, with the Mercedes team principal describing those positing such theories…
body: With Antonelli leading Russell by 84 points in the world championship as they go into this weekend’s Singapore Grand Prix, the Italian’s first title is within his reach. The 20-year-old has driven superbly in only his second season in F1 but Russell has struggled with poor fortune and reliability issues that have stymied his championship challenge.

At the last round, in Malaysia, an engine failure cost Russell a potential podium spot and led to a host of accusations online of bias towards Antonelli. Speaking in Singapore, Wolff’s exasperation was clear.

“They’re brainless, whoever thinks that, it’s completely nonsensical,” he said. “I don’t know what’s going on. Do they think I have a button that says: ‘George, engine failure now’? Or disadvantaging one driver against the other when we are fighting for a constructors’ championship when we have always had the mindset of providing everybody equal material?
points: Verstappen takes pole in sprint qualifying in Singapore.
With Antonelli leading Russell by 84 points in the world championship as they go into this weekend’s Singapore Grand Prix, the Italian’s first title is within his reach.
The 20-year-old has driven superbly in only his second season in F1 but Russell has struggled with poor fortune and reliability issues that have stymied his championship challenge.
“They’re brainless, whoever thinks that, it’s completely nonsensical,” he said.

highlights.title: I Really Want to Get Back into The Witcher 3 but I Have Save Game Anxiety
highlights.summary: It can be quite a hump to get over. You're not in the flow anymore, and the flow can be hard to find. You could always start again, but that means losing all of your previous progress.
body: You know the feeling, I bet you do. There's a game you played and loved but never finished — or never felt you got closure on, in one way or another. And, suddenly, there's a compelling reason to go back, like a patch or visual refresh. But trying to start a big, complicated game in the middle is disorienting and hard work. You have to remember how everything works, what the buttons do, what's happening in the story, what all this stuff in your inventory does, how you set up your character build, where the useful vendors are, and so on.

I'm in this position right now with The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. I'd like to go back to the game to check out all the changes and improvements in the new, free Remastered update. I'd also like to be poised and ready, immersed in the character of Geralt and his world, by the time the new expansion Songs of the Past drops next year.

But in this case, my dilemma is more complicated than choosing between picking up old threads or starting again. I've played this game a lot — mostly a long time ago — and started new saves a bunch of times. I've got a bewildering variety of starting points to pick from.
points: You're not in the flow anymore, and the flow can be hard to find.
You could always start again, but that means losing all of your previous progress.

highlights.title: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules
highlights.summary: The camera-maker says it is now re-evaluating the rules and procedures of its Small World in Motion contest.
body: The winner of a prestigious scientific photography competition has been disqualified following concerns raised by other scientists that it was fake.
Nikon said the use of generative AI in the composition of the video broke the rules of its Small World In Motion contest, which accepts photos and video taken using powerful microscopes.
The firm said the video "did not comply with the competition rules regarding generative AI", but added it was not a judgement of the entrant's professional reputation or scientific contributions.
It said it would now look at the rules and procedures of the annual contest, which has been running for 15 years and is specifically for microscopic images.

highlights.title: Even ‘Law & Order’ Is Terrified of AI
highlights.summary: In its 26th season premiere, the procedural legal drama paints a damning picture of power-mad AI CEOs.
body: Longtime fans of the NBC procedural Law & Order know that storylines often center around hot-button issues in the news cycle, often to absurdist effect (see: the episode brave enough to ask: “What if Paula Deen shot Trayvon Martin?” ).

It was inevitable, then, that the franchise would dip a toe into the wacky world of artificial intelligence. With its mercenary culture, power-hungry CEOs, and massive ethical and philosophical implications, the rapidly evolving AI industry is ideal fodder for the series. But while this week’s season opener is entertaining, the show’s foray into the AI space doesn’t say anything new or interesting about the technology. Instead it largely rehashes the dangers the public is already acutely aware of, until the very end when the stakes become startlingly clear.

highlights.title: I’m Still Convinced the iPod Was the Perfect Gadget
highlights.summary: Apple’s original music player got many things right. Chief among them: It didn’t connect to the internet.
body: I remember the birth of the iPod, 25 years ago this month. I was working at Newsweek. It was October 23, little more than a month after the attacks on the twin towers of the World Trade Center, and everybody was focused on the aftermath. I didn’t go to Cupertino for the launch, where Steve Jobs pulled the gadget from his jeans pocket and boasted that it contained a whole music library. Apple couriers hand-delivered the device to me in New York, and Jobs got on the phone with me. “iPod,” he told me, “will be a landmark product.”
He was right. By 2004, I was writing a cover story called “iPod Nation,” and later I published a book about the iPod called The Perfect Thing.

All these final dates were an inevitable consequence of what Steve Jobs put in motion on January 11, 2007. That’s when he announced three new products—a phone, an internet device, and “the best iPod ever,” all integrated into a new thing called the iPhone. From that moment on, the iPod as a separate device was living on borrowed time.

In a statement to Variety, a spokesperson for ReedPop wrote, “We are aware of a repeated disturbance from a fan in the audience during Thursday’s ‘Helluva Boss’ panel. We are taking steps to ensure any future incidents are addressed in a swifter manner.”
